data.title: HOW SOVEREIGNTY CHANGED ITS MEANING
data.subtitle: The same word — four different political realities across four centuries.
data.source: Krasner, *Sovereignty: Organized Hypocrisy* (1999); Evans & Sahnoun, *The Responsibility to Protect* (2001)

events.title: Westphalian
events.definition: The prince is sovereign within his borders. External powers have no legitimate authority inside another's territory. Sovereignty as territorial exclusivity.
events.keyPassage: "Cuius regio, eius religio" — whose realm, his religion.

events.title: Self-determination
events.definition: Sovereignty flows from the people, not the prince. Nations have the right to determine their own political status. Wilson's Fourteen Points fracture dynastic sovereignty.
events.keyPassage: "Self-determination is not a mere phrase. It is an imperative principle." — Wilson

events.title: Non-interference
events.definition: UN Charter Article 2(7): sovereignty as a shield against intervention. The great powers agreed to disagree — sovereignty as procedural equality between states.

events.title: Conditional
events.definition: Responsibility to Protect (R2P) reframes sovereignty as conditional: states that fail to protect their populations forfeit the norm's protection. Sovereignty as responsibility, not right.
